subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram partial-stream finalization lacks clear delivery-mode observability (sent vs preview-finalized vs canceled)

question: Should this issue stay scoped to the narrow Telegram delivered-state fix in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84563, or be broadened into the cross-channel final-delivery contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561 before implementation lands?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the issue also asks for delivery-mode taxonomy and an optional strict fresh-final behavior that affect Telegram product semantics and config surface.

options.title: Rebase And Prove The Telegram Fix
options.body: Keep this issue canonical for the Telegram partial-stream path, rebase or replace the linked PR, and require redacted live Telegram proof before closing.

options.title: Split Product Taxonomy From Bug Fix
options.body: Land the delayed delivered-state repair first, then track delivery-mode taxonomy or strict fresh-final mode as a separate maintainer-approved follow-up.

options.title: Fold Into Cross-Channel Contract
options.body: Treat this as a slice of the broader durable final-delivery contract and leave the Telegram-specific PR closed or replaced only after that direction is approved.

recommendation.title: Rebase And Prove The Telegram Fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical for the Telegram partial-stream path, rebase or replace the linked PR, and require redacted live Telegram proof before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history shows repeated lane-delivery and dispatcher ownership, and this decision spans Telegram streaming semantics rather than only one local line change.
